title: Ethiopian Spiced Cabbage
community: All of Ethiopia — the spiced cabbage of the everyday table
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Tikil Gomen — cabbage cooked with carrots, potatoes, onion, turmeric, and cumin. A staple element of the Ethiopian celebration and fasting platter — simpler and milder than Gomen, providing a gentle, familiar vegetable note.
longDesc: Tikil Gomen (literally 'spiced cabbage') is the most mild-mannered of Ethiopian vegetable dishes — the cabbage's natural sweetness, the carrots' beta-carotene, and the gentle spicing of turmeric and cumin make it a universally loved side dish. It appears on virtually every Ethiopian mesob.
steps: Heat oil. Cook onion until golden.
Add garlic, turmeric, and cumin. Stir 30 seconds.
Add potatoes and carrot. Stir. Add water.
Cover. Cook 8 more minutes until everything is tender.
chefTips: The cabbage wilts significantly — start with what seems like too much.
Add potatoes before cabbage — they take longer.
commonMistakes: Adding cabbage at the same time as potatoes.
cookingScience: See ETH105 for mixed vegetable science.
sustainabilityTips: Cabbage grows abundantly in Ethiopian highlands.
culturalNote: Tikil Gomen is the comfort vegetable of Ethiopian cooking — mild enough for everyone, familiar enough to welcome new guests, and present on virtually every Ethiopian table at every meal.
